Subject: Evidence request: pen test artifacts for Redwood Private in our VPC

Jordan —

Thanks for the quick onboarding call last week. Our SOC 2 audit team (A-Labs) has asked for the penetration test artifacts and a clear statement of the test boundary for the Redwood Private deployment running in our AWS account (BankCorp prod VPC us-east-1). Specifically they need: 

- The pen test report (redacted if necessary) that covers the most recent external/internal engagement you ran against the Private control plane and admin interfaces.
- A boundary diagram that shows which subnets and endpoints were in scope vs out of scope (management/control plane, model-serving workers, storage).
- Egress matrix: which external endpoints (S3, SageMaker, third parties) the deployment can reach outbound.
- Confirmation of whether the test included any targeting of customer-managed resources (peering/VPC endpoints) or if the scope was limited to Redwood-managed components.
- Any remediation evidence or tickets for findings that were classified as medium/high.

We also require a short note on redaction policy (we cannot receive raw hostnames/IPs without a data handling agreement). Can you confirm what you can provide and an expected delivery date? Our auditor wants the package by close of business 2026-10-16 to keep the audit timeline.

Thanks,
Samuel Lee
Director, InfoSec
BankCorp Financial

Subject: Re: Evidence request: pen test artifacts for Redwood Private in our VPC

Hi Sam —

Adding technical context on the boundary assumptions and what was (and was not) tested for the Private deployment in your account: 

1) Deployment topology (high level)
- Customer VPC contains model-serving EC2/GPU instances in private subnets.
- A small Redwood-managed control plane runs in a separate management VPC that communicates to the customer VPC over an egress-only, customer-initiated TLS channel (outbound to our control plane endpoints).
- There is no inbound route from the public internet directly into worker nodes; management plane access is mutually authenticated and initiated from the customer side.

2) Egress constraints during the test
- Default configuration uses AWS VPC Endpoints for S3 and ECR; outbound to the internet is restricted and uses NAT Gateway only for administrative operations.
- During the engagement, testers were granted scoped access to the management API (control plane) and the web-admin console only. Testers were not permitted to perform lateral movement into unrelated customer subnets outside of the Redwood-managed placement.

3) Bastion/Debugging access
- A temporary, timeboxed bastion (AWS SSM session manager) was used for repro and diagnostics; no long-lived bastion host existed.

4) Findings & remediation status
- SEC-4823 (privilege escalation via misconfigured role): mitigation deployed 2026-09-20, verification in progress.
- SEC-4971 (exposed debug endpoint - medium): patch scheduled, ETA 2026-10-20.
- SEC-5012 (info leak - low): closed 2026-09-15.

Weve attached an updated egress matrix (egress_matrix_v2.csv) that maps service endpoints observed during the test to the intended security controls. The full evidence packet will include sanitized logs and request traces; we will not include raw IPs unless covered by a data transfer NDA.

If your auditor needs an enumerated list of tested hostnames/ports for control validation, we can provide an attested list with IPs redacted and signed by our security lead.

-Karthik
Senior Infrastructure Engineer, Redwood Inference

Attachment stub: egress_matrix_v2.csv
